/-!
# Digit $2$ in base $3$ representation of $2^n$

*References:*
- [Some Unconventional Problems in Number Theory](https://doi.org/10.2307/2689842)
  by *Paul Erdös*, Mathematics Magazine 52, no. 2, p. 67, 1979
- [arxiv/2107.12475](https://arxiv.org/abs/2107.12475)
  **Hardness of busy beaver value BB(15)** by *Tristan Stérin, Damien Woods*
- [Hardness of Busy Beaver Value BB(15)](https://doi.org/10.1007/978-3-031-72621-7_9)
  by *Tristan Stérin, Damien Woods*, Reachability Problems, Lecture Notes in Computer Science
  15050, Springer, Cham (2024)
-/

namespace Arxiv.«2107.12475»

/--
For $n > 8$, $2^n$ is not the the sum of distinct powers of $3$. Expressed here in terms of the base $3$ digits of $n$.

This conjecture is equivalent to the halting of a $15$-state $2$-symbol Turing Machine.

TODO(lezeau): Formalize the Turing Machine version of this problem.

Source: *Hardness of Busy Beaver Value BB(15)*: https://link.springer.com/chapter/10.1007/978-3-031-72621-7_9
This is also https://arxiv.org/abs/2107.12475.
-/
@[category research open, AMS 5 11]
theorem CollatzLike (n : ℕ) (hn : 8 < n) : 2 ∈ Nat.digits 3 (2^n) := by
  sorry

/--
For $n = 8$, $2$ is not contained in the base $3$ digits of $n$.
-/
@[category test, AMS 5 11]
theorem two_not_in_digits_three_pow_eight : 2 ∉ Nat.digits 3 (2^8) := by norm_num

end Arxiv.«2107.12475»

findings.description: The docstring at line 37 says the conjecture is equivalent to halting of a 15-state, 2-symbol Turing machine. The cited machine instead halts exactly when the conjecture is false. Thus the positive conjecture stated by the Lean theorem corresponds to non-halting. The formal theorem itself is correct.
findings.source_evidence: Stérin–Woods, https://arxiv.org/abs/2107.12475, abstract and v2 Theorem 1: an explicit 15-state, 2-symbol Turing machine “halts if and only if Erdős’ conjecture is false.” The published abstract at https://doi.org/10.1007/978-3-031-72621-7_9 says the same.
findings.suggested_fix: Replace the sentence with: “This conjecture is equivalent to non-halting, on a blank tape, of the explicit 15-state, 2-symbol Turing machine constructed by Stérin and Woods.” Leave the Lean statement unchanged.

findings.description: The last sentence of line 35 says the formalization uses the base-3 digits of n, but the Lean expression is Nat.digits 3 (2^n). The source also concerns the digits of 2^n. These are different numbers: for the permitted value n = 9, n = 100₃ contains no 2, whereas 2^n = 200222₃ does. This is a documentation error only.
findings.source_evidence: Stérin–Woods, arXiv:2107.12475v2, Conjecture 1 (§1.1): “For all natural numbers n > 8 there is at least one digit 2 in the base 3 representation of 2^n.” Source: https://arxiv.org/e-print/2107.12475, main.tex lines 315–318.
findings.suggested_fix: Change “the base $3$ digits of $n$” to “the base $3$ digits of $2^n$”.

findings.description: The docstring at line 49 claims that 2 is absent from the ternary digits of n = 8. That is false: 8 = 22₃. The correctly proved Lean statement instead concerns 2^8 = 256 = 100111₃, which contains no 2. Both digit expansions were independently verified with norm_num in the scratch file.
findings.source_evidence: Erdős, “Some Unconventional Problems in Number Theory,” Mathematics Magazine 52(2) (1979), p. 67: “However, 2^8 = 256 = 3^5 + 3^2 + 3 + 1.” Read at https://www.renyi.hu/~p_erdos/1979-22.pdf. Stérin–Woods, arXiv:2107.12475v2, §1.2, explicitly gives 100111 as the ternary representation of 256.
findings.suggested_fix: Change the docstring to: “For $n = 8$, $2$ is not contained in the base $3$ digits of $2^n$,” or state directly that $2^8 = 100111_3$ contains no digit $2$. Leave the theorem and proof unchanged.

reformulations.difference: Lean uses membership of digit 2 in the ternary expansion, whereas Erdős’s original 1979 formulation says that 2^n is not a sum of distinct powers of 3. The arXiv paper explicitly adopts the digit formulation.
reformulations.equivalence_argument: Every ternary digit is 0, 1, or 2. Absence of 2 therefore means that positional expansion is a sum of 3^i over the distinct positions whose digits are 1. Conversely, a finite sum of distinct powers of 3 has coefficients 0 or 1, so no carrying occurs and its ternary expansion omits 2. In /workspace/review/equivalence.lean I proved, without the conjecture axiom, the general equivalence `(2 ∈ Nat.digits 3 m) ↔ ¬ ∃ S : Finset ℕ, (∑ i ∈ S, 3^i) = m`, and then the equivalence of the universally quantified conjectures for n > 8.

sources_consulted: https://arxiv.org/e-print/2107.12475 — v2 LaTeX source, especially Conjecture 1, Theorem 1, §§1.1–1.2, and the halting-equivalence proof
Paul Erdős, Some Unconventional Problems in Number Theory, Mathematics Magazine 52(2) (1979), pp. 67–70, especially p. 67; read at https://www.renyi.hu/~p_erdos/1979-22.pdf
https://www.renyi.hu/~p_erdos/Erdos.html — bibliography identifying the original article as 1979-22
review.notes: Both formal theorem statements are faithful; all findings concern documentation only. The research-open tag agrees with the latest cited arXiv version and the published abstract. Nat.digits has its ordinary positional meaning at base 3, and 2^n is always positive, so its empty/zero conventions do not affect the claim. Independent Lean checks proved the boundary examples and all permitted cases below 30; evaluation for 0 ≤ n < 500 found exactly the expected exceptional exponents [0, 2, 8]. The existing test proof has no sorryAx dependency. Experiments are in /workspace/review/scratch.lean, boundaries.lean, and equivalence.lean; the reviewed file was not modified.
